<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Hitesh Soliwal and Contributors to the Synexia Project -->
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
# Finite resource comparison plan

Execute only after the component semantic, API and actual-JNI gates finish. All
processes run sequentially, after other compilation and test workloads stop.
Every invocation retains its exact argv, exit, stdout, process statistics and
SHA-256. Use identical generated probe bytes against the sealed compiled owners.
Never rewrite a product or fixture to obtain a favorable measurement.

The fixed VM settings are a 64 MiB initial heap, 256 MiB maximum heap, 256 KiB
thread stack, Serial GC and two reported active processors. Checked-JNI behavior
has a separate gate; resource invocations consistently omit `-Xcheck:jni`.
The core lane uses the available source-built M3 runtime with the selected
classes patched into java.base. The SDK lanes use the same Temurin 21.0.8+9
runtime as component compilation. Neither lane is a complete current-source
M3JDK21 image qualification.

For each workload group use two consecutive, balanced fresh-VM blocks: baseline,
candidate, candidate, baseline; then candidate, baseline, baseline, candidate.
Retain first-call observations separately from warmed samples. GNU time records
whole-process user/system CPU and maximum resident set; those values include VM
startup, fixture preparation, verification and compiler activity and are never
presented as operation CPU.

## Comparisons

1. Core pass00 against pass03: the exact generated M3IndexAtomResourceProbe at
   sizes32,4096,32768 with3000,400,100 measured operations respectively. This
   fixture measures allocated bytes and elapsed nanoseconds, not per-operation
   thread CPU. Compare each workload separately and check deterministic final
   checksums across lanes. The three selected owners are independent workloads.
2. SDK pass04 against pass05: M3ArrayifiedIndexResourceProbe, both using the same
   candidate native library. This isolates the index-owner source edit. The
   fixture validates expected arrays, warms each operation2000 times, then emits
   five1000-operation samples at32 and4096 positions, with allocation and
   current-thread CPU counters.
3. SDK pass05 against pass06: M3BitmapOccurrenceRefinementProbe resource JAVA
   and NATIVE_REQUIRED, each with256 repetitions per warmed sample. The fixture
   measures14 sizes, four masks and three warmed samples, and separately records
   the first call per fixture. Projection preparation and correctness checks are
   outside the timed operation. Both lanes use the same candidate native library.
   The unchanged native and below64 paths are controls, not claimed improvements.
4. Native compactor pass00 against pass04: a separate frozen, reviewed resource
   plan covers both actual JNI two-mask window entrypoints. Its baseline and
   candidate share the same Java class files. Instrumented transfer counts and
   UBSan execution remain separate evidence from actual JNI timing.

## Decisions

Summarize raw samples and per-workload medians; preserve all samples, including
unfavorable results. Allocation reductions and exact transferred-byte counts
are independent of wall-clock noise. A new optional path is not admitted on
allocation alone if repeated CPU observations show a material regression. A
consistent regression above10% triggers a focused confirmation using the same
fixture and flags; it is not discarded as noise. A confirmed regression vetoes
that optional transformation. Ambiguous or noisy timings remain observations,
not a speed claim. Do not select only favorable masks, sizes or fresh processes.

The result is a finite host/workload comparison. It does not establish a
universal speedup, whole-product memory/energy improvement or platform parity.
